admission.justification: Prefix removal and no removal at all were weighed and rejected, and the exact-name list now binds the product, the sandbox tooling and every future harness whose names are added.

alternatives.option: The product holds one exact-name list of session identities; every host start removes those names and keeps logins and credentials; the sandbox tooling reads the product's list and adds its own.
alternatives.reason: Exact names remove exactly the session ties and leave OAuth tokens and home selectors intact; one list keeps the product and the fixture from drifting.

alternatives.option: Remove variables by the CLAUDE_ and CODEX_ prefixes.
alternatives.reason: Prefix removal would also discard logins, configuration and credentials of those harnesses, which sessions need.
alternatives.reconsider_when: No harness login or configuration lives under those prefixes.

alternatives.option: Remove nothing; let the host inherit and pass on the starter's environment.
alternatives.reason: An agent started by such a host re-enters the starter's session and the host keeps state the user did not choose to give it.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The host stops handing its own environment to the agents it starts.

consequences: A running host that carries a listed name is left running and named by status; the remedy is paseo stop and a start at a time the user chooses.
The list's coverage of harnesses nobody has listed yet (Pi, Hermes, Cursor) stays an open truth gap.
context: The Paseo daemon keeps the environment of the process that started it and hands it to every agent it starts; this machine's supervisor carried CODEX_* names and the dashboard carried CLAUDE_* and PASEO_* ones. The sandbox tooling already removed a list of exact names and its docstring states the rule.
decider: architect's refinement under D75, frozen in MIK-R96@v1 rule 10
